requirement: Check exactly one public package and one exact version per invocation; no local manifest or runtime is needed.

An explicit --version must identify one release; reject ranges, moving tags and filesystem dependencies. Swift maps an exact version to one verified release tag; do not accept arbitrary branch/tag selectors. Canonical public Swift package URLs are identity input only. Otherwise use only the declared metadata provider default; if absent return review. Never search for an older or alternative release.

Fetch metadata through the single declared ecosystem adapter (deps.dev by default; Pub and Swift require dedicated adapters) and query OSV for the canonical ecosystem/name/version. Never execute a package manager or project code during check.

Built-in minimum age is 14 elapsed UTC days. Optional .gh-dependency-pulse.cue supplies minAgeDays for both commands; explicit --min-age-days overrides it, including zero. Require a nonnegative integer; zero disables age checking only. Check remains usable without configuration or Git.
Known applicable non-withdrawn advisories or deps.dev isDeprecated=true yield fail. This is an upstream deprecation signal; do not claim comprehensive yanking or retraction coverage.
Missing release/default, missing required date, future date, too-young release, incomplete response or provider failure yields review. No registry fallback chain.

Pass requires confirmed release metadata, sufficient age and a complete OSV query with no active findings. Fail takes precedence over review; review takes precedence over pass. Both fail and review block install.
Follow OSV page tokens up to 10 pages with repeated-token detection; any incomplete query yields review unless a fail is already known. Ignore withdrawn advisories; deduplicate remaining IDs.

Use a 30 second overall check deadline and 10 second HTTP request timeout with context cancellation; no retries or persistent cache in v1. Bound each response to 10 MiB; oversized or malformed responses yield review.
Install invokes the same check service and policy once. Only pass may launch a native tool using the checked exact version. No override flag or silent version substitution.

Execute a validated argument array without a shell in the invocation working directory; inherit environment and stdin. Keep stdout and stderr connected to the corresponding native streams. Own check/launch diagnostics go to stderr. Stream both immediately without whole-process buffering, prefixes or JSON wrapping; preserve their content. No total order between streams is promised.

Propagate native exit status and cancellation; startup failure returns nonzero. After a passing check and before declaration edits or delegation, verify the selected manager/launcher is available. If missing, exit 1 with its name, one or two lines of macOS installation guidance and an official installation URL. No automatic tool install, tool fallback, native output parsing or wrapper success message.

Native tools own resolution, lockfiles, scripts and partial changes on failure. A bounded tested declaration adapter may insert the exact checked dependency when a required manager has no suitable native add operation. No preflight resolution, transitive scan, staging, rollback or repair. Preserve normal native configuration, credentials and lifecycle hooks; no custom Python environment management.

One check service, normalized release/result model, policy evaluator, OSV client and process runner serve every language. Small internal metadata adapters and descriptors isolate provider identity; manager descriptors/argument builders isolate installation. Language-specific policy branches are forbidden.
No retained legacy modes or compatibility schemas. No repository stars, owner counts, Scorecard, identity verification, typosquatting lists, plugin framework or per-language policy branches.

Only public packages from declared supported sources are in scope. Dart, Swift and Kotlin are required alongside Go, Python, Rust, TypeScript and JavaScript; Java check remains required. Additional languages follow independent check/install priorities in language-support.csv. Private registries remain excluded. Unsupported capabilities fail before network access.
Own output must not expose credentials, raw HTTP bodies or untrusted instructions. Render upstream names and identifiers as bounded plain text with terminal control characters escaped.

Each supported language has one default manager. Resolve language/manager aliases into canonical ecosystem plus selected manager; preserve manager identity even when checks share an ecosystem. Canonical ecosystem output is alias-independent. No environment-based manager selection or fallback; missing tools fail clearly. Kotlin uses Maven checks and Gradle installation; Java/Maven install is optional.

Use the same check/install command shape, flags, policy, result schema, reason codes and exit contract for every language. Package coordinates may vary; users need not know native manager flags. Install checks once and reports native success/failure without claiming runtime compatibility or additional security verification.

Promote cheap optional check and install capabilities independently through descriptors and shared fixtures. Never enable install merely because check works; never treat a candidate matrix row or OSV ecosystem presence as implemented support. Required adapter design gaps must be resolved before claiming delivery.

Within a Git boundary (.git file or directory), discover the nearest optional .gh-dependency-pulse.cue from cwd upwards through the boundary directory inclusive. Without a Git boundary, inspect only cwd and ignore ancestor configuration. Load only one file; explicit CLI values override file values, which override built-ins. Invalid present configuration exits 2 before network or execution. Keep native installation cwd unchanged.

Project format accepts json or markdown and defaults to markdown for check and list. Explicit --format overrides it. List also accepts table via the CLI. On check --json aliases --format json. Reject conflicting output flags. Configured JSON must not affect install streams; install rejects explicit formatting flags.

Recommend latest stable tools without version enforcement, latest-release lookups or automatic upgrades. Respect pinned wrappers/toolchains; older installed versions are not rejected by age alone. Manager availability checks are independent of package-version selection and minimum-age policy. Check never probes local managers.

List direct dependencies for the explicitly selected ecosystem from conventional invocation-relative manifest paths only. Do not execute tools or traverse projects; optional lockfiles supply version evidence only.
Provide JSON, Markdown and table with uniform package, requirement, exact version and scope fields. Keep unknown versions and partial listings visible.

Without --check list is offline. With --check reuse standalone verdicts, age, latest version and advisory details for exact eligible releases. Missing exact versions or unsupported sources produce review without a provider request.
Standalone check reports nullable age_days/latest_version and advisory IDs with available titles. Latest lookup is best effort and cannot affect the exact-release verdict or change package selection.
